7.0     CABLE CONSTRUCTION

            In  addition  to  the  technical  requirements  stated  in  the  previous  section,  the

            constructional requirements specific to all the power and control cables as described

          below  shall be  followed.  Sections  applicable  for  particular  voltage  ranges  are

          mentioned against those. Other sections are common for all voltage ranges.

          7.1  Conductor

              Conductor shall be annealed, circular, stranded tinned  / metal coated copper,

              smoothly drawn, free from defect, complying with the requirement of IEC-60228.

             The conductor class (min. class 2) shall be selected to obtain the desired bending

                radius as per clause no 7.9.

          7.2  Conductor Insulation

              Conductor insulation  shall be extruded insulation made out of Cross linked

             compounds (EPR / HEPR / XLPE only) complying with the requirements of IEC–

              60502.

           7.3    Internal Construction (for High Voltage Cables  - 3.6 / 6 (7.2) kV and above)

             7.3.1  Cables rated 3.6 / 6 (7.2) kV and above shall be provided with non-metallic

                   extruded semi conducting compound screening, to be applied on top of a

                   semi-conducting tape for conductor and extruded nonmetallic semiconducting

                     layer in combination with a metal layer as insulation screening over each core

                    as per IEC 60092-354. The dimensional, physical and electrical requirements

                    of the metallic layer (metallic screen) shall be determined as per IEC 60092-

                   354.

             7.3.2  The fillers, binders and extruded inner covering shall be of non-hygroscopic

                     material, shall be suitable for the operating temperature of the cable and

                   compatible with the insulating material and shall be provided as per IEC

                 60092 – 354; the thickness of inner covering shall be according to IEC 60092

                 – 354 (for extruded). The inner covering shall be extruded cross-linked

                    elastomeric halogen free compound (SHF 2).




 FORMAT No.             Ref. PROCEDURE No.           ISSUE No.                 REV. No.                    REV. DATE:
OES/SOF/028                                                          03                        00                           26.02.2018

      OFFSHORE                                           Rev. No.   5                       FOR ELECTRICAL POWER AND

       SERVICES
                                                           Page: 6 OF 10


          7.4   Internal Construction (for Low Voltage Cables - 0.6 / 1.0 (1.2), 1.8 / 3 (3.6)

                   kV).

              For above mentioned voltages, cores of a multicore cable shall be laid up and the

                 interstices  filled up with non-hygroscopic  fillers & extruded non-hygroscopic

               inner covering shall be provided as per IEC 60092 – 353. The material selected

                 shall be compatible with cable components with which  it  is in contact and

              compatible with the operating temperature of the cable. A suitable binder is to be

                to be applied before application of the extruded inner covering. The thickness of

               extruded inner covering shall be according to IEC 60092–353. The inner covering

                 shall be extruded cross-linked elastomeric halogen free compound (SHF 2).


          7.5  Armouring

             Armouring shall be selected to as to achieve the bending radius requirement of

               clause7.9.Multicore  cables  shall be mechanically  protected with  hot dipped

               galvanized steel wire braiding (GSWB) or galvanized round steel wire armouring

             (GSWA).Single core low voltage and high voltage cables shall be mechanically

               protected with tinned phosphor bronze wire braiding (PBWB) or hard drawn

             aluminium round wire armouring which shall be applied over the inner covering to

              confirm to the requirements of international standards. In cases where the steel

             armour layer is required to comply with a minimum conductance, it is permissible

                to include sufficient copper or tinned copper wires in the armour layer to ensure

              compliance. The armour of single-core cables for use on a.c. circuits shall consist

               of non-magnetic material. In special cases, for instance when the cables are used

             on d.c. circuits, magnetic materials can also be used.

          7.6  Outer Sheath

            The outer / over sheath shall be heat and oil resistant, suitable for installation in an

               offshore oil and gas processing platform. Material for outer sheath shall be cross-

               linked elastomeric halogen free compound (SHF 2) extruded in one or more

                closely adherent layers as per IEC 60092-350.

              7.7.2    Fire resistance cables shall be in compliance with IEC 60331-11 & 60331 -

                       shall be provided over the conductor, before the insulation.

           7.9  Bending Radius

              Cables shall be flexible and suitable for installation with the minimum bending

                 finalized based on installation contractor’s requirement.

8.           Cable Drums

             8.1  Cables shall be dispatched on suitable barrel diameter, securely battened, with

                   takeoff ends of the cable brought to the outside of the drum (either wooden or

                   metallic) and fully protected against mechanical damage.

             8.2  Besides customary markings as per any prevalent standard / code, each cable

               drum shall be fitted with a stainless steel or equivalent corrosion resistant label.

               The label shall be fixed to the outside of each flange, engraved with the

                  following information:

                 i)    Cable Manufacturer’s name
                  ii)   Cable type number
                  iii)  No.  of  cores  and  cable  cross   sectional   area   in mm  and  core
                   construction/stranding e.g. 3C+E 4mm2, (7/0.85)
              iv)   Voltage grade
             v)    Standard(s)
              vi)   Purchase order number/item number
               vii)  Cable length (in metres)
                viii) Net and gross weights (kg)

 9.       Cable Accessories

            9.1 Cable termination kits for use on high voltage systems shall be suitable for the

                type of cables offered as per this specification. The terminations shall be supplied

                  in kit form. The terminations kit shall include all insulating and sealing materials

                 apart from conductor fittings and consumable items. The Contractor shall ensure

                   that installation instructions are included in each kit.

            9.2 Cable termination  kits  shall be provided with semi conductive de-stressing

                 appropriate for the working voltage.

            9.3 The cable terminations kits shall be suitable for terminations of the cables to an

                 indoor-switchgear, weatherproof enclosure, outdoor transformers or hazardous

                 area motor terminal box, as the case may be. The terminating kits shall be

                 heat/shrinkable sleeve type.

            9.4 The Contractor shall provide type test certificates for cable termination kits as

                per IS 13573 from the manufacturers of these kits for review by company.



  10.    INSPECTION AND TESTING

            10.1    General

            10.1.1 The cable shall be tested and inspected at the manufacturer’s works, or at a

                   recognized testing facility. The Contractor shall ensure all the test equipment

                   necessary to test the cables is provided by the manufacturer. Test certificates

                     for all tests shall be provided to the Company, immediately on completion of

                       tests performed. All tests shall be witnessed by the Company or its authorized

                     representative.

            10.1.2 Company shall be advised at least (4) weeks in advance of the scheduled date

                   of each test and again 20 days prior to the actual test.

            10.1.3 The Contractor shall ensure detailed records and log sheets regarding the

                      results of the tests and certification are furnished for review.

            10.1.4  The Contractor shall furnish all necessary information concerning the supply

                      to the Company’s inspector or representative. The inspector shall have free

                     access to the manufacturer’s works for the purpose of inspecting the process

                     of manufacture in all the stages and will have the authority to reject any

                     material which appears to be unsuitable or of unsatisfactory quality.

            10.2    Testing

            10.2.1 All LV Electrical cables shall be tested in compliance with the IEC standard

                 60092-353 and HV cables shall be tested in compliance with the IEC standard

                  60092-354. In case cable is tested as per other international standards (IEEE,

                  BIS, NEMA or NEC), the tests shall be either equivalent to IEC or more

                      stringent. After installation, tests will be carried out for cables with lower

                   voltage rating in accordance with IEC 60502-1 and for cables with higher

                   voltage rating, in accordance with IEC 60502-2.

            10.2.2 For type tests, valid type test certificates certified by any reputed international

                 agency are acceptable in lieu of tests. Type test certificates must be submitted

                     to company representative / inspector during inspection.


            10.3    Sealing

                  Immediately after electrical tests, the ends of the cable shall be sealed with

                    heat shrink caps to prevent the ingress of moisture.

 11.0    CERTIFICATION

          All  cables  and  cable  accessories  of  similar  design  and  construction  features
          manufactured by the same Vendor:

               a)    Shall have been type tested by an authorized testing agency/lab viz. CPRI,
            ERDA etc.
              b)   Shall be having current certification/approval/listing by UL/FM/ATEX/IECEx
                       etc.

        1.0 SCOPE:

          The intent of this specification is to define the minimum requirements for explosion proof
             control stations  / push button stations to be located near the motors on the offshore
             platforms.

        2.0 CODES AND STANDARDS:

           2.1 The following codes and standards shall form a part of this specification:

            NEC               -     National Electrical Code.

           NEMA           -     National Electrical Manufacturer’s Association.

                BSI               -      British Standards Institution.

                API-RP-14F    -    Recommended practice for design and installation of
                                              Electrical system for offshore production platform.

                 API-RP-500     -      Classification of areas for electrical installations at
                                                drilling rigs and production facilities.

                BIS               -     Bureau of Indian Standard

            2.2 Any other recognized international code or standard may be used in lieu of above
                with prior approval of the Company.



        3.0 SITE CONDITIONS:

            All materials shall be selected and finished to resist/withstand the site conditions
            Specified in General Design Criteria enclosed in the Bid Package.

        4.0 SCOPE OF SUPPLY:

          The scope of supply includes.

            4.1 Explosion proof control stations / push button stations of various types.

          4.2 Cable lugs & explosion proof double compression type nickel chromium plated brass
              cable glands.

       5.0  TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:

          5.1 The control stations / push button stations shall be explosion proof and weather-proof
                suitable for operation in class-1, Division-2, Group-D or Zone 1, Group II A/II B, and
               temperature Class T-3 (200ºC). Their enclosures shall be explosion-proof to NEMA-7
             and weather-proof to NEMA- 4 (IP-56) or equivalent.

         5.2 They shall be made up of cast metal aluminum alloy with offshore painting as per ISO
            12944-6 / high impact strength glass polyester material housing complete with requisite
              terminals and explosion-proof cable termination accessories suitable for cable as per FS
             4011. If aluminum is used, the same shall be copper-free. The glass polyester material,
                   if used, shall not get damaged due to ultra-violet rays over its life span.

         5.3 Contact for push buttons shall be rated for 6 Amps. At 240VAC. AC-11 duty and   4.0
          Amps at 11OV D.C., DC-13 duty.

         5.4 Wherever start-stop push buttons are used, the start push button shall be Momentary close
             type while the ‘Stop’ push button shall be stay put type and lockable in pressed condition.
           The colours of push buttons shall be as follows:

                  Start:  Green (Shrouded)

               Stop:  Red (Mushroom head type)

          5.5 Auto - Manual / local - Remote Selector switches shall be knob type having Stay-put type
              contacts of rating same as that of push buttons. Auto - Manual / Local - Remote switch
            and start - stop pushbuttons, wherever required, shall be housed in a common enclosure.

          5.6 The control stations shall have four lugs for mounting on the pre-fabricated available
              supports. The lugs shall be off-set so that the rear surface of the Unit stays at least 5 mm
           away from the surfaces. On lugs, two holes shall be round and two oblong to facilitate
               correct positioning of the control station.

          5.7 Desired number of terminals plus 10% spare shall be provided for connection of external
              cable    leads    of    copper    conductor.    Necessary    cable    termination

              accessories shall be supplied with each control station. The cable entry shall be from the
             bottom. These entries shall be properly plugged to protect the equipment during transit.

          5.8 1 No. external Earth terminal shall be provided on the body.

          5.9 A nameplate indicating the equipment to be operated shall be provided for each control
                station. The particulars of the nameplate will be furnished later. Nameplates shall be of
                stainless-steel having letters of a minimum height of 5 mm.

        5.10Warning  inscription “ISOLATE ELSEWHERE BEFORE OPENING”  shall  be
             prominently and indelibly displayed on the top cover of control stations.

       5.11Ammeters  shall  invariably  be  incorporated  in  the  control  station  for  motors
               irrespective of  their KW ratings and sizes. Ammeter scale shall be suitable to read both
              rated current and starting current.

        5.12 A red mark shall be provided at the full load current of the motor, the values of which
               will be furnished along with the Purchase Specification to the successful vendor.

        5.13 The control stations shall be tested and certified as defined in Electrical Design Criteria
             enclosed in the Bid Package. Each equipment shall have certification mark on  its
             nameplate.

        5.14 All control stations shall be provided with canopy of suitable material and proper size
               for protections against rain, fog etc.

        5.15 All hardware such as nuts, bolts, washers etc. shall be Cadmium / stainless steel plated.

                 present according to the order and the packing list.
            6.1.2 A visual inspection shall be made to ensure that good workmanship and practices
              were adopted during fabrication and assembly.

    7 SPARES:

         7.1 Vendor shall recommend and provide spare parts needed for start-up. In addition, vendor
              shall also furnish a separate price list of recommended spares for two (2) years of normal
            operation and maintenance.

        7.2 Recommended spares shall take into account related factors for system reliability, effect
            of downtime upon production, safety, cost of parts and availability of equipment service
               facilities.

        7.3 All spares furnished by vendor shall be wrapped and packaged so that they could be
            preserve in original as new condition under the normal conditions of storage prevailing in
             India and shall be properly tagged and coded to facilitate future identification. They shall
           be packaged separately, clearly marked as "Spare Parts", and shipped along with the
             control / push button station. Packing lists shall be furnished so that the parts can be
           handled without uncrating, if required.

      11 CERTIFICATION:

            All Control Stations / Push Button Stations offered or those of similar design and

            Construction features manufactured by the same vendor:

               • Shall have been type tested by accredited laboratory / Institution.

               • Shall have been in continuous satisfactory service in offshore for a minimum  period

            two years,

               • Shall be having current certification / approval / listing UL / FM /ATEX / IECEX /

          CPRI OR ERDA.


      12 PACKING AND TRANSPORT:

          The control station / push button stations along with their accessories shall be shipped to
             Site packed in wooden crates. They shall be wrapped with polythene Sheets, before being
            placed in the crates to prevent damage to finish. Crates shall have skid bottom for
            handling.

1. SCOPE

   This specification covers the minimum requirements for cable transit system to be
   used on offshore platforms.

2. CODES & STANDARDS:

    2.1. The cable transit system shall comply  to the requirements of   the latest
        revisions of relevant standards/ directives of:

        DNV    :  Det Norske Veritus.
           API      :  American Petroleum Institute
           IEC      :   International Electro-technical Commission.
           ISO      :   International Standard Organization

    2.2. Any other recognised international codes or standards may be followed in lieu
        of above with prior approval of the Company.

3. SITE CONDITIONS:

    All cable     transit    systems    shall be designed to    withstand    the     site
    conditions specified elsewhere in the Bid Package.

4. SCOPE OF SUPPLY:

   The scope of supply through this specification includes:

    (a) Insert blocks or modules.

    (b) Frames.

    (c) Any required accessories such as gaskets, lubricants, stay plates etc required for
       proper installation of cable transit system.

5. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS:

    5.1. General:

       The cable transit system shall be tested and certified for fire integrity and gas
         tightness.

    5.2. Material of construction: Cable transit frames shall be made of stainless steel.

    5.3. Fire Integrity:

       The cable transit frames shall have minimum class of A60 (SOLAS) or EI
       60(BS EN 13501-2). Transit system modules or  insert blocks shall have
          certified for fire ignitability as per ISO 11925-2 or equivalent.

    5.4. Gas tightness: The cable  transit system shall be rated for minimum gas
        tightness as stipulated in “DNV: Type Approval Programme for Cable and
       Pipe Penetration” or equivalent.

6. TESTING AND INSPECTION:

   Testing & inspection of the cable transit system shall include but not necessarily be
    limited to the following:

    6.1. Visual inspection.
    6.2. Verification of Type Test reports

        intimation of at least 20 days shall be given to enable the Company to depute
          its representative to witness the test.

    the cable transit system supplied under this specification and provide necessary

    8.2.   Copies of type test certificates shall be provided.

9. CERTIFICATION

    All cable transit system offered shall be having current certification/approval/listing
   from UL or FM or by an agency approved by the Company.

1. SCOPE

   The scope of this specification is to define the requirements of LED light fixtures and
    junction boxes suitable for installation in unclassified areas on offshore platforms.

2. CODES & STANDARDS

    2.1. The items shall be in accordance with the latest applicable Codes and Standards
        of :

     NEC    -     National Electrical Code

    NEMA -     National Electrical Manufacturer’s Association

      BSI     -      British Standards Institution.

      ANSI   -    American National Standards Institute

      BIS     -     Bureau of Indian Standards

      IEC     -      International Electrotechnical Commission

     ATEX  -    Atmosphere Explosible

      IESNA -     Illuminating Engineering Society of North America

3. SITE CONDITIONS

    All light fittings, junction boxes and their accessories shall be designed to
   withstand the site conditions specified in the General Design Criteria enclosed
    in the Bid Package.

4. SCOPE OF SUPPLY

   The scope of supply through this specification includes:

         LED Light Fixtures complete with driver circuit.

         Junction Boxes

         Cable glands, plugs etc.

         Clamps, Brackets etc. for fixture supports.

5. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

    5.1. General :

        5.1.1.  All indoor LED light fittings and junction boxes (located in enclosed
             rooms) shall be industrial/decorative type with enclosure protection to IP-
              22,  as  minimum.  They  shall  be  provided  with  shrouding  type
               terminals/live parts to make them shockproof, while cleaning, replacing
                 etc.

        5.1.2. The body of junction boxes shall be Stainless steel (SS) and shall be free
            from frictional sparking hazard. Copper or copper alloy shall not be used
               for manufacturing of any exposed parts.

        5.1.3. The LED light fittings and junction boxes shall be suitable for mounting
            on   poles/ceiling/columns.   Suitable  Clamps/brackets   required   for
                installation shall also be supplied.

        5.1.4.  All the lighting fixtures/junction boxes shall be provided with internal
               earthing terminal and external terminals as per IS/IEC 60079-0.

        5.1.5.  Double compression type nickel/chromium plated brass cable gland and
              tinned copper crimping type lugs shall be provided for all LED light
                 fittings and junction boxes.

        5.1.6.  All LED light fittings and junction boxes nameplates shall bear the stamp
              of certifying agency.

        5.1.7. The LED  fixtures  shall be high  efficiency,  durable, rugged, with
         minimum lumen depreciation and designed for ambient temperature of 45
           deg C. The fixtures shall have been type tested in a NVLAP (National
           Voluntary Laboratory Accreditation Program, USA) accredited laboratory.

              (1) As per LM-79 (IESNA) for
                      Total Luminous Flux
                      Luminous Intensity Distribution
                       Electrical Power Characteristics
                      Luminous Efficacy (calculated)
                      Color Characteristics
            (2) As per LM-80 (IESNA) for lumen maintenance and LED lifetime
                projections shall be made using TM-21 method.
            In Situ Temperature Measurement Test (ISTMT) temperature shall be used
           while generating LM-80 report and TM-21 projection. The LEDs shall have

    5.2. Light Fittings

              block the unused entries.

        5.3.2.  Adequate no. of the terminals shall be provided to terminate three cables.
               Sufficient space for accommodating specified No. of cables and easy
              access to their terminals for termination purposes, shall be provided.

        5.3.3.  Four plugs shall be provided for mounting of junction box on wall/steel
               structure with the help of bolts.

    6.1. Testing and inspection of light fittings and junction boxes shall include but not

     A visual inspection shall be made to ensure that the finishing and workmanship

 1.0  SCOPE

      This Specification defines the minimum requirements for design, manufacture, supply and

       testing of electrical cable glands and accessories for high voltage and low voltage systems for

      armoured and non armoured cables on the offshore process / well platforms.

 2.0  CODES AND STANDARDS

       2.1 Codes Standards and Regulations:

           All cables, accessories and other components supplied,  shall comply with the  latest

           revisions of the applicable codes and standards.

                  IEC               IEC 60079.

                         British Standard     BS EN 50262

              B I S                Bureau of Indian Standards


           Further the Contractor shall ensure all mandatory Indian statutory requirements are

          complied with.

 3.0    SITE CODITION

         All the cables and accessories shall be designed to withstand the conditions specified in the

         General Design Criteria enclosed elsewhere in the bid package.

 4.0   SCOPE OF SUPPLY

        The Scope of this specification includes the following items:

          4.1      The complete cable gland system including body, washer, nut, seal etc.

 5.0   TECHNICAL REQUIREMENT

      GENERAL:

         5.1 All cable glands shall be made of brass and finishing shall be nickel plated.

         5.2 Cable Glands shall be double compression type except where soft bedded cables i.e.

             typically fire resistant are used. For such cables the sealing method should be chosen to

            avoid cold flow. Examples of such types are displacement and diaphragm types.





FORMAT No.             Ref. PROCEDURE No.           ISSUE No.                 REV. No.                    REV. DATE:
OES/SOF/028                                                         03                        00                           26.02.2018

=== PDF PAGE 140 ===
                                                             Spec. No.  FS 4043                            FUNCTIONAL
      OFFSHORE                                           Rev. No.   1                            SPECIFICATION FOR
       ENGINEERING                                             Discipline  Electrical
                          ELECTRICAL CABLE       SERVICES
                            GLANDS            Page: 3 OF 4

         5.3 To meet the ingress protection requirement the space between cable glands, adapters and

            blanking elements and the enclosure shall be sealed by means of a sealing washer or

            thread sealant.

         5.4 The cable gland shall be selected to match the cable diameter. The use of sealing tape,

            heat shrink tube or other materials is not permitted to make the cable fit to the cable

             gland.

      FOR CLASSIFIED AREA:

         5.5 Cable glands, when installed shall not invalidate the specific characteristics of the type

            of protection of the electrical equipment on which they are mounted.


         5.6 Cable glands shall be in accordance with IEC 60079-0 and shall be selected to maintain

             the requirements of the protection technique according to Table 10 of IEC 60079-14.

         5.7 Where glands are used for unarmored cables in a hazardous area, care should be taken to

            ensure that they are able to fulfil the requirements of IEC60079-0. Where the product has

             limitations denoted by an X on the certificate, additional measures should be taken to

            secure the cable.

         5.8 The cable entry system shall comply with one of the following for Ex ‘d’ equipment:

                a) Cable glands sealed with setting compound (barrier cable glands) in compliance

                 with IEC 60079-1 and certified as equipment;

               b) Cables glands with IEC 60079-1 and are certified as equipment

          5.9  Cables glands and accessories  shall be  suitable  for operations without periodic

              maintenance applied throughout the life span of the equipment.

         5.10 Units and information.

               All quantities and dimensions shall be expressed in metric units. All information,

              manual, certificates, data and inscriptions shall be in the English language.


 6. INSPECTION AND TESTING

           (a) Test certificates for all cable glands shall be provided to the Company.

          (b) Random inspection of cable glands installed at yard or site shall be carried by company

              or authorized representative.

        GENERAL

          Scope

           This specification covers the design and engineering of instruments, control systems,
             accessories and materials, along with special test equipments, where the supply is part of
           an offshore project. This specification is general and all instruments/systems included
         may not be required for the proposed project. The scope shall be as defined in Scope of
           Supply of Instrumentation.

1.1.2      The detailed Scope of work, Specific Job requirements, exclusions, deviations, additions
               etc. if any, will be indicated in Scope of Supply of Instrumentation and Job Specification
             of Instrumentation included in Requisition/Tender.

1.1.3      This specification provides only the qualitative specifications of commonly used
            instruments. Specifications of Instruments not covered in this specification shall be
            submitted by bidder for review by Purchaser.

1.1.4       Bidder shall be fully responsible for design, material selection, sizing and selection of the
           proper instruments for their system. The compliance to this specification does not
            absolve the bidder of the responsibility towards contractual obligations with regards to
           completeness, proper selection, satisfactory operation and easy maintenance of the
            platform/package.

1.1.5       All instruments and control systems, Distributed Control System (DCS), Programmable
           Logic Controller (PLC) and othet system oriented items' like Multiphase Flow Meter ,
          Water Cut Meter, machine monitoring system, speed governor control, antisurge /
           performance control system, analyser system etc. offered shall be field proven and should
           have completed trouble free satisfactory operation for a period of minimum 6 months on
           the bid due date in a similar application in offshore installation with the process
            conditions similar to those specified in Purchaser's datasheets. Items with proto-type
            design or items not meeting provenness criteria specified above shall not be offered.

1.1.6       In the event of any conflict between this specifications, data sheets, related standards,
           codes etc., bidder shall refer the matter to the purchaser for clarification and only after
            obtaining the same should proceed with the manufacturing/engineering of the item in
            question. DCS/PLC specifications is not included in this document. Bidder shall refer
            Standard specifications for DCS and PLC attached separately in case DCS and PLC are
            included in Scope of supply.

1.2        Applicable National / International Standards

1.2.1       Design, terminology and selection shall comply, as a minimum, with the latest edition of
            following codes, standards and publications.

       AGA      American Gas Association, Gas Measurement Committee
                       Report No.3   Orifice Metering of Natural Gas and Other Related
                                 Hydrocarbon Fluids — Concentric, Square-Edged Orifice
                                    Meters
                       Report No.7   Measurement of Natural Gas by Turbine Meter

 2.0      DESIGN PHILOSOPHY

 2.1         All field as well as control room instruments shall be suitable for use in a humid and
             tropical offshore climate. These shall be furnished with all necessary weather and
              anticorrosion protection to prevent damage from saline and corrosive process atmosphere.
         PLCs and Control Systems located in local panels shall be suitable for continuous
            operation in specified ambient temperature and humidity conditions without any
              deterioration in performance.


 2.2        Statutory Approvals

              a) Bidder shall be responsible for obtaining all statutory approvals, as applicable, for all
                instruments and control systems.

                i) For all intrinsically safe / explosion proof / flameproof equipments / instruments/
              systems or equipments with any other type of protection allowable which are
               manufactured abroad and certified by any statutory authority like Laboratorie Central
             Des Industries Electriques (LCIE), British Approval Service for Electrical Equipment
                in Flammable Atmospheres (Baseefa), Factory Mutual (FM), Underwriters
                 Laboratories (UL). , ATEX, CIMFR etc.

                  ii) All instruments Panels and Junction Boxes located in open deck areas shall be
                   certified for use in Class I, Division 1/ Zone 1 area irrespective of the actual hazardous
                area classification. The methods of protection shall generally be as specified below.
            Any alternative method, if required due to any special technical reasons, shall be used
                only with a categorical approval from Purchaser.
                1) All field transmitters and valve positioners shall be intrinsically safe type based
                 on entity concept Intrinsic safety shall he achieved by means of external Intrinsic

              2)  All process switches shall be flameproof certified to NEMA 7/ Ex d. Solenoid

              3)  Junction boxes shall be flameproof to NEMA 7 / Ex d for explosion-proof

               The above Instruments and JBs shall be Weatherproof (NEMA 4X/ IP 65

                 by Bidder for each instrument and control systems.

               5)  All panels and cabinets installed in classified area shall be flameproof as per
            NEMA 7/ Exd, as a minimum.

 2.3    All signals to and from central control room shall be electronic. The standard analog signal
         shall be 2 wire, 4-20 mA DC Smart HART Type having superimposed digital signal for both
         transmitters and control valve positioners.

 2.4     Electrical control and alarm switches shall have SPDT snap acting micro switches rated for
       110V/240V AC, 5 AMPS and 24 VDC,1 amps and shall be suitable for 'inductive load. Limit
        switches shall be proximity type only.

 2.5     Instrument ranges shall be selected such that the normal operating point is middle third of the
       instrument total range. Standardisation of such items as scale ranges, length of level
         gauges/level controllers shall be considered.

 2.6     All level instruments on vessels/tanks shall have flanged connections. All inline instruments
         including control valves, flow instruments etc shall have flanged end connections. Standpipes
        wherever applicable shall be provided with isolation valves.


 2.7    Nozzle requirement for Temperature Instruments
        a)  The nozzle projection on vessels for all instruments and nozzle length for temperature
             instruments on piping will be minimum 8" and to be verified during detailed engineering
              stage.
        b)  For Thermowell installation, minimum pipe size shall be 4". Less than 4" pipe size shall
            be blown upto 4".

 2.8    Tube fittings shall be of the double ferrule, pressure seat, no torque type for use on heavy or
         thin wall tubing.

        Instrument materials shall be resistant to highly corrosive marine saline atmosphere. The case
         material of all instruments shall be SS 316. Wherever SS 316 is not available, epoxy painted
      Copper Free Aluminium (Cu content < 0.4%) cases suitable for offshore corrosive
        environment shall be provided. Mounting accessories for all instruments shall also be SS 3316
         or superior material. Canopy shall be provided for all electronic type instruments (transmitters
     & positioners), Fire & Gas devices and junction boxes, panels located in open or under grating
         area to protect from rain and sun without impairing access or visibility.

2.10      Use of asbestos, mercury, lead and cadmium in instruments shall be prohibited due to
            hazards associated with them.

2.11       Connection for air or gas supply, transmission and control signals shall normally be
              internally threaded 1/4" NPT.

2.12        Instruments process measurement connections shall be threaded 1/2" NPT minimum.

2.13      Shutdown shall be actuated by independent tripping devices with independent tapping
             points & independent instrument root valves.

2.14       Terminals for electrical connections including thermocouple extension wires, shall be
          numbered and identified to indicate polarity, ground connections, test connections and
           any other pertinent information.

2.15       Terminal blocks shall be non-hygroscopic. Vibration proof and shall use captive screws
             for terminals. Terminals shall be tinned or Silver-plated. All terminations shall be through
            use of wire lugs.

2.16        All venting instrument including solenoid valves and pilot valves shall have bug screens
               fitted to atmospheric vents.

2.17        All moving parts exposed to atmosphere such as linkages, bellows, springs and coils shall
          be resistant to the atmospheric conditions Cadmium plating is not acceptable for this
             service.

2.18        Instruments shall be supplied in sealed heavy plastic bags containing desiccant material
            during shipment. All parts, subject to moisture, shall be suitable for tropical conditions.

2.19        All electronic instrumentation shall be immune to RF interference due to walkie-talkie,
           paging system, communication system etc. Also all electronic modules shall be designed
             for protection against short circuit.

2.20     A means for calibration of transmitters, indicators and transducers shall be provided to
            permit adjustment of the zero output and span output. Calibration and alignment of all
            instruments shall be performed by the manufacturer before shipment.

2.22        Field Transmitter

2.22.1      Pneumatic Field Transmitter

2.22.1.1    Pneumatic Transmitters, indicators, controllers and transducers shall meet the following
            requirements
                 i)   Reference accuracy shall equal or better than ±0.5% of span. Controller output
                    indications shall be better than ±2% of span.
                 ii)    Hysteresis shall not exceed ±0.5 % of span.
                 iii)   Repeatability shall not exceed ±0.5 % of span.
              iv)   Output change caused by 100°F temperature change shall not exceed ±1% of span.

2.22.1.2    Pneumatic Transmitters shall be generally force balance type. The transmitters shall have
           an integral indicator.

2.22.2    SMART Field Transmitter

2.22.2.1    Electronic transmitters shall be SMART type with 4 - 20 mA DC output with
           superimposed digital signal having simultaneous analog and digital communication.
          Communication protocol shall be HART only. The following specifications shall also
             apply:
                i)    Transmitters shall be provided with external zero & span adjustment and shall have
                     integral vent/drain.
                 ii)   All transmitters shall be provided with integral intrinsically safe output meter
                 having LCD display. The transmitter shall be microprocessor based and it shall
                   incorporate a non-volatile memory which shall store complete configuration data of
                   transmitter. All necessary signal conversions, including conversion to produce
                   output with the required protocol shall be carried out in the transmitter electronics.

                 iii)   Transmitter shall also run complete Sub-diagnostic routine. In the event of
                   detection of failure, the output shall be driven to predefined value, which shall be
                      field configurable.
              iv)   Temperature sensors shall be provided to compensate for process temperature and
                 ambient temperature variations.

            v)   The transmitter shall be able to assure an accuracy of ±0.065% of span for a
                   rangeability of 1:10. The accuracy shall include the combined effect of linearity,
                    hysteresis and repeatability. However, for diaphragm seal instruments, the accuracy
                   of ±0.25% is acceptable.

             c)  Corrosive process conditions.

            d) Viscous & congealing liquids.

 3.0     GENERAL SPECIFICATION OF FIELD INSTRUMENTS

 3.1       Flow Instruments
 3.1.1 "     General

 3.1.1.1     Generally a Piezoelectric/ Capacitance type Electronic Smart transmitter coupled with
               orifice plate flow element shall be used for flow measurement. Variable area meters may
            be used for conditions described in 3.1.2.2.

 3.1.1.2    The static pressure element shall be connected to the downstream pressure tap on gas
           flow measurement. The static sensing point shall be independent of the differential
             sensing points.

 3.1.1.3      Differential pressure instruments shall withstand maximum pressure equal to full line
             pressure without zero or calibration change.

 3.1.2      Primary Element

 3.1.2.1     The standard primary measuring element shall be a concentric orifice plate designed for
             flange taps except for particular process requirements.

            Quadrant edge or quarter circle orifice plates shall be used for highly viscous liquids and
              for pipe Reynold number below 10,000.

 3.1.2.2     Variable area flow meters

 3.1.2.2.1    Variable area flow meters may be used when:
             a) Only local flow indications required.

             b) Linear flow rate signal characteristics are required.

             c) Extremely low flow rate measurement.

            d) Rangeability greater than 3 to 1 and as identified in P&ID.

3.1.2.2.2    Linear-scale rotameters shall be marked for direct reading of flow and manufacturer shall
             furnish a guaranteed calibration curve.                                                    •
3.1.2.2.3     It shall be metal tube type except for non hazardous, non toxic and non viscous service
            such as Instrument air / Nitrogen service where glass tube can be used.

  3.1.3     Measuring Instruments

          Where orifice, flow nozzle, venturi, averaging pitot tube is used for flow measurement,
              Differential Pressure transmitters shall be generally used. A five (5) valve manifold with
            proper drain connections shall be utilised with differential pressure instruments.

3.1.4      Range Selection

3.1.4.1     The orifice meter differential range shall be 500, 1250, 2500 or 5000mm of water (20, 50,
          100 or 200 inches of water). The range 2500 mm (100 inches) is desirable wherever
              possible.

3.1.4.2     For orifice meters the normal flow should be between 60% and 80% of the meter
          maximum.

3.1.4.3     For rotameters / variable - area flow meters the normal flow rate shall be between 50%
           and 80% of the instrument range.

3.1.4.4      Multistage Restriction Orifice shall be considered for high pressure drops. Thickness of
             Restriction Orifice shall be selected based on the presSure drop for each stage:

3.1.5       Orifice Flanges

3.1.5.1      Orifice flanges shall be in accordance with piping classification with a minimum flange
              rating of ASME 300 class and for 11/2" and below line size integral orifice with meter run
           assembly shall be considered. Two pairs of flange taps located diametrically opposite
              shall be provided for each orifice assembly.

3.1.5.2   D — D/2 taps should be considered for line size greater than 14".

3.1.6       Orifice Meter Runs

3.1.6.1      All meter runs shall be designed for flange tap differential.

3.1.6.2      Orifice fittings which permit changing of the orifice plate without interrupting the flow
            through the pipeline and without the use of a bypass shall be used, wherever necessary.

3.1.6.3     The piping layout, wherever possible, should be arranged so that straightening vanes are
             not required.

3.1.6.4        It is preferred that metering orifices be located in horizontal lines. Sizing of Orifice shall
           be as per AGA 3 Standard for Natural Gas service and ISO 5167 standard for liquid
              service. Upstream and downstream straight lengths shall be as per applicable codes and
             standards.

3.1.6.5      Orifice meter runs shall not be less than 11/2 inch nominal pipe size.

3.1.6.6     Mating flanges shall be so aligned that jack screws will be diametrically opposite.

 3.1.6.7    Senior Orifice Plate Assembly

            Senior orifice assembly shall include as a minimum supply of orifice plates, plate carrier,
            flanges, senior orifice fittings, studs, bolts, nuts, hand wrench and plugs. Senior orifice
              fittings shall include sliding valve, equaliser, stuffing box and sealing unit and all other
           system to make the system complete. Senior orifice assembly shall be flanged at both ends.

         The orifice plate rangeabilty is to be taken as 1:3 while deciding the number of plates
            required to cover the required range. In addition, adequate overlap should be provided
           between two consecutive flow ranges.

            Straightening vanes with meter runs required shall be provided by vendor. Straightening
           vanes shall be flanged type. Upstream and downstream straight lengths for orifice plates
              shall be as per applicable sizing codes and standards (AGA 3/ ISO 5167).


3.1.7        Positive Displacement Flow Meters

3.1.7.1     Flow Meter / Transmitter

3.1.7.1.1   The following performance characteristic shall be satisfied as a minimum by the flow
             transmitter:

                  Repeatability of ± 0.05 % of reading in the rated linear flow range.

             -  Accuracy of ±0. 2 % over the rated flow range
             -  For high accuracy applications Positive Displacement Flow meter having accuracy of
              ±0.1% shall be provided

3.1.7.2     The flow direction shall be clearly stamped or cast on the body.

3.1.7.3     The flow meter shall have an over-range protection of at least 130%.

3.1.7.4      Pick up coil shall be hermetically sealed.

3.1.7.5   PD Meter shall be used for high viscosity and congealing services. PD meter shall be
            provided with strainer and air eliminator in crude oil service and wherever necessary. The
               air eliminator shall be supplied complete with pressure gauge, safety valve etc. and shall be
             located upstream of strainer.

3.1.7.6      Strainer shall be provided with Differential Pressure Gauge for choked flow indication.

3.1.7.7     Each Positive Displacement meter shall be calibrated using a suitable method as per API-
        MPMS.

3.1.8      Turbine Meters

3.1.8.1     Turbine meter output shall be 4-20 mA dc / pulse with power supply 24V DC. Necessary
             preamplifier shall be provided integral with meter. Local electronic totalizer, transmitters
            (pulse to current converter) with 4-20mA dc output shall be provided. Accuracy for the
            turbine meter shall be ±0.2% of FSD. For high accuracy applications, Turbine meters
           having accuracy of ±0.15% shall be provided. Turbine meters shall have flanged end
             connections.

3.1.8.2     Output for turbine meter shall be compatible with the control room instrumentation.

3.2        Pressure Instruments

 3.2.1       General

3.2.1.1     The following considerations should be applied in the selection of pressure instruments:

            a)    Pressure gauge measuring element shall generally be the Bourdon tube type. For
                measurement of slurries, viscous and corrosive fluids, diaphragm seals shall be
                   used.

            b)   Case material for all Pressure gauges, transmitters, switches shall be SS 316.

             c)   Gauges and instruments shall be capable of withstanding 130 % of the maximum
                   range.

            d)   Gauges and instruments subject to damage from pulsating pressures shall be
                  provided with snubber type pulsation dampeners. Gauge savers (Pressure Limiting
                 Valve) shall be provided wherever necessary for protection of the pressure gauge.
                   Material shall be 316 SS or better as required for the service.

             e)    Indicating scales shall be direct reading in engineering units.

        0    Ranges shall be selected so that the normal operating pressure will be in the middle
                     third of calibrated range.

 3.2.1.2    The process sensing point shall be Iodated in an undisturbed pressure zone with the
             pressure instrument located as close as possible.

 3.2.1.3      Pressure Switches shall be avoided as far as possible except for packages where there are
            space constraints. Pressure switches shall have field adjustable set points. Adjustments
             shall be internal and tamper proof. Electrical pressure switches shall have set point
               indicator.
 3.2.1.4     For pressure differential instrument a (5) Five valves manifold or a (3) valve manifold
            with proper drain connections shall be provided.

 3.2.2       Controller

 3.2.2.1     Local controllers shall be pneumatic if identified in the P&ID for well platforms and shall
            normally include adjustable proportional band plus reset action and auto-manual bypass
             assembly.

 3.2.2.2    When blind pressure pilots are used, indicating pressure gauges shall be mounted adjacent
              to the pilot for indication of pilot output.

 3.2.3       Pressure Gauges

 3.2.3.1      Pressure gauge case shall be liquid filled type with external zero adjustment.

 3.2.3.2     Case diameters shall be 6" (150 mm).

 3.2.3.3      Instrument air/gas supply gauges used as output gauge may have 50 mm (2") dials.

 3.2.3.4    Movement shall be 316 SS and 1/2" NPT bottom connection.

 3.2.3.5     Accuracy shall be ±1 % of full scale.

3.2.3.6    Gauges shall have micro-meter pointers and white dial with black numerals and

3.3        Level Instruments

3.3.1       Displacer type Level instrument to be avoided. Guided wave Radar type Level
              transmitters to be used as fas as possible. Non Contact Radar type Level transmitters to be
            used where service is viscous, congealing or cryogenic. Radar Antenna shall be selected
          by vendor based on process conductivity suitability and the dielectric constant. Echo
             rejection circuit shall be provided in Non contact radar electronics. All Radar level
           instruments shall be provided with local digital level indication. All Radar level
             instruments shall be provided with diagnostics in control room. Guided wave radar shall
           be external type except where vessel conditions/ dictates otherwise.

3.3.2       External displacer cages shall be supplied with side/side connections. Where this is not
             possible top/ bottom or side/ bottom connections may be provided. Displacer instruments
              shall be Torque Tube type construction.

3.3.3        Differential pressure level measurement is acceptable for remote level indication for level
            range of 1524 mm (60") and above. Seals and wet leg compensation shall be provided as
             required. These instruments shall have zero elevation/ suppression adjustment wherever
              required.

3.3.4       External displacer connections on transmitters/ switches shall not be common with other
             service connections, such as water drain or pump-out lines.

3.3.5       All level instruments in toxic and hydrocarbon service shall have blow down connections
              to a closed drain.

3.3.6        Rotatable heads shall be provided for displacer type instruments.

3.3.7       For external cages, block valves are to be installed in horizontal position of both lines at
             the vessels. If a vertical nozzle is used the valve shall be arranged so that no sediment
            pockets are present. A valve shall be installed to permit draining each displacer cage and
            piped to drip pans or deck drains.

3.3.8       Units for level indicating scales shall be- 0-100 percent.

3.3.9       Liquid Level Switches

 3.3.9.1      Field mounted level switches shall be avoided as far as possible. Field level transmitters
              shall be used for alarm and shutdown.

3.3.10     Tank Gauges

3.3.10.1    Level instruments for pressure and non-pressure storage tanks where measurement is not
              for accounting purposes, may be by differential head measurement or by a float and tape
            type level gauge. Float and tape type level gauge measurement accuracy shall be ± 2 mm.
           For remote transmission or difficult congealing, viscous, corrosive, high temperature
              services, cryogenic services etc., non-contact Radar type Level transmitters to be used.

 3.3.11     Magnetic Level Gauges

 3.3.11.1    Type of level gauges shall be magnetic only. Body (Float chamber, Float, Float Guide
            tube & spring assembly) shall be of minimum 316 SS with SS or Aluminium indicating
             tube with flapper colour change design.

 3.3.11.2     Float design i.e. its type, size & material requirements shall consider worst case process
            conditions also like specific gravity, temperature & pressure specified in process
              datasheets.

 3.3.11.3    Where magnetic level instrument is specified as external mounting type, the instrument
              shall be provided complete with external cage (float chamber).

 3.3.11.4     Float chamber or cage shall be provided with 3/4: flanged end vent & drain connections.

 3.3.11.5    The design shall also facilitate float removal.

 3.3.11.6    Mechanism to prevent float rotation &float damage due to rubbing against the chamber
             wall shall be provided.

 3.3.11.7    Flanges of Magnetic level gauges shall be minimum SS316, Carbon steel flanges shall
             not be used. End connections shall be threaded to NPT as per ASME B1.20.1, Flanged as
             per ASME B 16.5 & Grooves of ring type joint flanges shall be octagonal as per ASME B
             16.20.

 3.3.11.8    Orientation of measurement of scale for the offered magnetic level instruments shall be
                site adjustable to any angle without hot working/ welding.

 3.3.11.9   The design shall ensure that the magnetic properties of the applicable parts of the
           magnetic level gauge shall not degrade under the influence of the design temperature
            given on datasheets.

 3.4        Temperature Instruments

 3.4.1      General

 3.4.1.1      Filled thermal systems with armoured capillary shall be used for local mounted
          pneumatic transmitters, temperature switches (only as per package vendor
            recommendation) and controllers. Capillary tubing lengths over 8 meters (25 feet) shall
           not be used. Each thermal system shall be selected to withstand the maximum
             temperature to be encountered. Mercury filled system is not permitted.
 3.4.1.2   RTD type temperature sensing elements are to be used for all electronic temperature
              transmitters and measuring systems. The sensing element shall be Platinum 100 ohms at
           0°C to IEC 60751, 3 wire system.

 3.4.1.3      Electronic Temperature transmitters are to be head mounted at the sensing source with
           two wire transmission to the central control room. The output signal shall be 4-20mA DC
             with superimposed digital HART signal.

            Pressure Relief Valves

           General

          The basis of the selection of pressure relieving devices shall be in accordance with the
            requirements set forth in the API Standard, RP 520 and the latest revisions of the ASME-
           Power Boiler Code", and the ASME' "Code for Unfired Pressure Vessels, as well as local
             codes.

3.5.1.2     Venting and breathing equipment for low pressure above ground storage tanks shall be in
            accordance with API Std. 2000.

3.5.1.3     All pressure relief valves shall be marked and Certified in accordance with the ASME
             Boiler and Pressure Vessels Code.

 3.5.1.4      Lifting levers and bellows shall be specified as service requirements where codes dictate.
              Lifting lever shall be provided for all valves in air services and hot water services.

 3.5.1.5      Testing for tightness shall be in accordance with API RP 527.

 3.5.1.6      Pressure Relief valves sizing calculations shall be furnished to purchaser for review and
             approval.

 3.5.1.7      All safety relief valves shall be provided with test gag.

35.2      Types and Materials

 3.5.2.1      All relief valves of size 1" and above shall be full nozzle full lift type. Relief valves with
              size less than 1" shall be modified nozzle type.

 3.5.2.2      Relief valves 1" and larger shall be of the type having a nozzle bushing which extends
           through and beyond the base of the inlet bolting flange, and which forms the gasket
             bearing surface for the inlet flange.

 3.5.2.3     Flanged relief valves for process piping, excluding steam and air pressure piping, shall be
               either the enclosed spring type or pilot-operated type.

 3.5.2.4     Conventional valves shall be specified for constant back pressure while bellows seal type
            valves shall be specified for variable back pressure more than 10% of set pressure or
           where the service is corrosive. Pilot operated pressure relief valves shall be used for
             special services and where set pressure is closer than 10% of the operating pressure, in
              general. Balanced bellow materials shall be SS 316L or superior material.

 3.5.3       Connections

             3/4" X 1" thermal relief valves may have screwed ends. For variable back pressure and
             viscous services, size of thermal relief valves shall be 1" X 2" with D orifice. All process
                relief valves 1" size and larger shall have flanged inlet and outlet connections The outlet
            flange of relief valves discharging into closed systems shall be at least equal to the
             pressure rating of the outlet system at operating temperature.

 3.6.1       Control Valve Selection

3.6.1.1      In general, control valves shall be sized for maximum flow at not more than 90% opening
             of the valve and normal flow around 70% opening of the valve.

3.6.1.2     For Two-phase flow the control valve CV shall be the summation of the CV of the Liquid
            phase and CV of the vapour phase. The quantities and physical properties of liquid and
            vapour should be established on the outlet conditions of pressure and temperature.

 3.6.1.3     Valve bodies should be the maximum size required for any anticipated operating
             condition. If a substantial increase in future flow rate is indicated, reduced valve trim
              shall be used.

 3.6.1.4     Control valve sizing calculations shall be furnished for review and approval.

 3.6.1.5     Standard control valve body sizes are 1, 11/2, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14 and 16 inches. Valves
            with 21/2 inch and 5 inch body size shall not be used.

 3.6.1.6     Globe valves shall be used where throttling is required.

 3.6.1.7      Butterfly valves may be used when low pressure loss and high capacity flow is desirable.

 3.6.1.8     All control valves must have sound levels less than 85 db at 1 meter from valve. Source
            treatment shall be performed for noise control as far as possible. For very high noise
              levels Source treatment in conjunction with Path treatment shall be performed.

 3.6.1.9      Anti-cavitation trims shall be provided for valves with cavitation in liquid service.

 3.6.2       Control Valve Trim Characteristic

 3.6.2.1     Equal percentage characteristic shall be used in most applications where throttling is
              required. Other characteristics such as linear or which fall between the two shall be used
          when special types of valves, such as butterfly or ball valves, are specified.

 3.6.2.2     Quick-opening/ closing trim shall generally be used for on-off service.

 3.6.2.3      Control valves used in safety shut down service shall be single seated tight shutoff.

 3.6.3      Guiding

            Generally valves shall be single seated for viscous, congealing services or where clogging
             of cage can occur, Small single-seated valves and angle body valves may be stem-guided.
           Cage guiding shall be used in clean gas service.
 3.6.4      Shutdown Valves

 3.6.4.1     Shut down valves shall be of Flanged Full Bore Ball Valve with actuator.

 3.6.4.2     All Shut down valves shall be certified Fire safe as per API 607/ ISO 10497 by a
            recognized Third Party Testing agency. For Christmas tree valves (API6A), API 6D
             valves and metal seated valves, API 6FA certification is also acceptable.

 3.6.4.3     Shut down valves shall be Soft seated type with Class VI tight shut-off as per FCI 70.2.
            Rate A as per ISO 5208 shall be provided where specified in data sheets. For triple offset
              butterfly valves, Zero leakage valves shall be considered.

 3.6.4.4      Actuator type shall be spring return piston type with Quarter turn operation.

 3.6.4.5    Hand wheels shall not be provided on Shutdown Valves unless specified in

 3.6.7.3     The smart positioner shall provide HART protocol of latest version and shall be suitable

 3.6.7.4     In addition to operational and maintenance data provided by the positioner like actual

 3.6.7.5    The positioner shall also have built-in manual stroke button for stroke open or close the

 3.6.7.6      Valve's operating signatures in the form of hard copy and soft copy shall also be provided
              for each control valve.

 3.6.7.7     Valve Positioners shall have minimum two nos. Air/Gas gauges.

 3.6.7.8      Air/gas-filter/regulator shall be factory mounted on the control valve yoke.

 3.6.8       Actuators and Accessories

 3.6.8.1     Actuators shall be sized for control valves and shutdown valves at shut-off pressure
             indicated in Process Data Sheets. Actuators shall be painted green for fail open service
           and red for fail close valves.

              permits.

          requirements. Valve sizes and manifold arrangement shall be as per API
            recommendations.

 3.6.11.2    The bypass valve shall be correctly sized for the process requirement and when fully open
              shall not permit an excessive flow beyond the capability of the relief system.

 3.7       Flame Arrestors

          Body shall be with retractable element bank. End connections shall be flanged. Weather
           hood shall be provided, wherever necessary. Flame arrestor shall be designed as per ISO
           16852 and certified by a recognized Third party testing agency.

           proven in offshore application. In general analyser and sampling systems shall be
            designed and constructed in accordance with API standards, as applicable.

 3.8.3        Material of all components wetted by sample shall be 316 SS or superior material for
             general applications and Monel for Sea Water applications.

               ISO VG46 and ISO VG32.
                   Tests to be carried out are:

 10.6.11.1   Proof Pressure Test

            Test assemblies (tubes and fittings) selected at random shall be subjected to a pressure of
            1.5 times the maximum working pressure applied at the rate of 200 kg/cm2 per minute
           and maintained at the final pressure for five minutes without leak.

 10.6.11.2   Dismantling and Re-assembly Test

       A minimum of three test assemblies that have successfully completed 'Proof Pressure
              Test' as above shall be disassembled and assembled ten times after which they must pass
             the 'Proof Pressure Test' again.

 10.6.11.3  Hydraulic Impulse Cum Vibration Test

       A minimum of three test assemblies that have successfully completed the 'Proof Pressure
              Test' shall be mounted on a hydraulic impulse cum vibration test bench. They shall be
             subjected simultaneously to pressure impulse of 1.5 times the maximum working pressure
               at 30 to 100 cycle per minute and vibration in two mutually perpendicular planes at 1300
             to 2820 cycles per minutes for a minimum of 5 X 10 pressure impulses and 20 X 10
             vibration cycles. The only retightening is after the first 1000 pressute impulses to allow
              for bending. During the testing the leakage shall not exceed lcm3/Hr/Assembly.

 10.6.11.4  Vacuum Test

       A minimum of three test assemblies that have successfully completed the 'Proof Pressure
              Test' shall be subjected a negative pressure of 700m Bar and then disconnected from
          Vacuum Pump. The assembly must maintain the vacuum pressure for fifteen minutes.

 10.7       Instrument Cable Trays

 10.7.1      All cable trays and accessories shall be made of the fibre glass and shall be corrosion
              resistant and fire resistant (Class 1, Fire rating). The cable trays shall be designed and
           manufactured meeting the requirements of NEMA FG I, IS-6746 and ASTM E-84
             standards. An additive material shall be mixed with the fibre glass to make them resistant
              to ultraviolet light.

 10.7.2     The minimum glass content in FRP material shall be 45%.

 10.7.3     The ladder type trays shall have side rails and horizontal rungs. Both of these shall be of
          same material i.e. the Fibre glass with additive. The rungs shall be placed 300 mm apart
           from each other.

 10.7.4     The cable trays shall be supplied in standard lengths of 3000 mm and clear width of trays
               shall be 150,300,600 and 750 mm.

 10.7.5     The inside depth of the cable trays shall not exceed 150 mm.

 10.7.6     The tray construction shall have high degree of finish and shall be such as to facilitate
            easy handling and also to ensure easy laying of cables without causing damage to cables.

11.0      INSPECTION AND TESTING REQUIREMENT

           Requirements of non-destructive testing like,' radiography, magnetic particle test,
            hardness test, hydrotest for items such as control valves, safety valves, orifice flange
            assembly, level gauges etc., shall be carried out strictly as per respective piping class.
            For all instruments, welding and testing shall be carried out as per piping specifications.
             Post weld heat treatment shall be carried out for all weldings of instrument as required in
            accordance with the requirements of piping material specifications.

 11.2       For items like control valves, shutdown valves, pressure relief valves, desuperheaters etc.
           radiography procedure and area of casting to be radiographed shall be as per ANSI
           B16.34 and acceptance criteria shall be as per ANSI B16.34 Annexure B, in general.
          However areas of casting to be radiographed for type of valves/desuperheaters not
            covered in ANSI B16.34 shall be in line with ANSI B16.34.


          100 % radiography shall be done on the following areas of each item requiring
             radiography:-
                      Inlet flange neck
                   Outlet flange neck
                     cast nozzle (in case of safety valves)
                   All weld joints
         Two shots shall be taken for each area to be radio graphed, as a minimum.

 11.3       Following test shall be carried out by bidder at vendor's works and test certificate shall be
              furnished.

 11.3.1      Material test certificate including NACE requirements for all instruments and items.

 11.3.2       *Calibration/ test certificates for all instruments including control valves, safety valves.

 11.3.3      *Seat leakage test for control valves and shutdown valves.

 11.3.4      *Test certificate for safety valve set pressure and reseat pressure.

 11.3.5      *Hydrotest certificate for all inline instruments, pipes, tubes, fittings etc.

 11.3.6     *Radiography of control valve and pressure relief valves of rating ASME 600 Class or
             above.

 11.3.7      Conformity certificate from sub-vendor.

 11.3.8      Capacity certificate for control valves duly approved by third party.

 11.3.9    NACE compliance certificate.

 11.3.10    Fire Safe certificates for Shutdown valves

             All tests prefixed by (*) shall be witnessed by owner/owner representative /third party.
           The above is minimum requirement. Inspection agency engaged for the job shall detail
            out inspection and detailed testing procedure for individual items after contract is
            awarded.

  1.0     GENERAL
 1.1       This specification defines the minimum requirements for installation and testing of
             Instruments and Controls for Offshore.
  1.2      The bidder shall carry out the work in accordance with the codes, standards &
           recommended practices listed in Instrumentation Design Basis/ Criteria, Instrumentation
           Job Specifications, Standard Specifications, this Specification, and any "Statutory
             Regulations".
  2.0      APPLICABLE NATIONAL/ INTERNATIONAL STANDARDS
          The installation of instruments and controls shall comply, as a minimum, with the latest
              editions of following codes and standards:

           API        American Petroleum Institute
                RP 14C Recommended Practice for Analysis, Design, Installation and
                                   Testing of Basic Surface Safety Systems for Offshore Production
                                   Platforms
                RP 14F Design, Installation and Maintenance of Electrical Systems for
                                 Fixed and Floating Offshore Petroleum facilities for unclassified
                                and Class 1, Division 1 and Division 2 locations
                 RP 14G Recommended Practice for Fire Prevention and control on Fixed
                                open type Offshore Production Platforms
                 RP 14FZ Recommended Practice for Design, Installation and Maintenance
                                   of Electrical Systems for Fixed & Floating Offshore Petroleum
                                        Facilities for unclassified and Class 1 Zone 0, Zone 1 & Zone 2
                                      locations
                RP 552 Transmission Systems
          IEC          International Electro-Technical Commission
                      60079     Electrical Apparatus for Explosive Gas Atmosphere

          ISA          International Society of Automation
                    S 7.0.01   Quality Standard for Instrument Air
                        S12.13    Part I: Performance Requirements, Combustible Gas Detectors
                                     Part II: Installation, Operation and Maintenance of Combustible
                              Gas Detectors
                        S12.15    Part I: Performance Requirements, H2S Gas Detectors
                                   Part II: Installation, Operation and Maintenance of H25 Gas
                                    Detectors

       NEMA      National Electrical Manufacturer's Association

 3.0     INSTRUMENT INSTALLATION REQUIREMENT
            Bidder is responsible for installation of all items in their scope of supply including supply/
             fabrication of all installation/ erection material. The scope of installation shall include
            instruments on platforms, Package item instrumentation, Pneumatic shutdown panels,
             control system instruments like Hardwired Relay Based Control Panels, Local Control
             Panels etc. as required to complete the project in all respects.
          The bidder shall prepare hook-up and installation detail drawings based on indicative
           hook-up drawings regarding each type of instrument for Purchaser's approval and shall
              carry out the installation in accordance with these approved drawings.

          The bidder shall install instruments and equipment with due consideration of the
             following:

 Format No. 8-00-0001-F1 Rev. 0                                                   Copyright EIL — All rights reserved

  3.1      No instrument with the exception of pressure gauges and temperature indicators shall be
              installed in such a way that it depends for support on the impulse piping or electrical
             connections to it.
  3.2         Positioning of equipment shall not constitute a safety hazard. Where possible, instruments
             shall be mounted so that they are protected from the effects of rain and sun, while
            maintaining the requirements for access and visibility. Bidder shall provide canopyfor all
             instruments (electronic type) and junction boxes located in open or under grating areato
              protect from rain and sun without impairing access or visibility.
  3.3       Ease of access shall be provided for lifting heavy items or equipment such as valves,
             panels etc.
  3.4        Instruments shall be mounted/ connected so as not to stress vessel nozzles or pipe
              tappings. Isolation valves for maintenance purpose shall be provided for standpipes.
 3.5        Instruments shall be properly supported on brackets or mounted on sub-plates or placed on
           a suitable pedestal, pipe stand or structural support. Pipe or structural stands may be
           welded directly onto platform plate, with a suitable penetration in the grating, where
              applicable.
  3.6         Instruments, tubing, cables and cable ladder shall not be fixed to gratings or handrails.
 3.7         Fittings such as instrument isolating valves and instrument air or gas regulators shall be
            supported either on the instrument stand or close-coupled to the instrument in a manner
               that no undue stress is imposed on the tubing or instrument.
  3.8        Separate local panels for Instrumentation and Electrical shall be considered as far as
              possible. Instrument stands or panels shall be in accordance with the approved drawings,
            with consideration for:
             a)    The direct routes for minimum tubing and piping to and from the stand, using
               common tubing runs and avoiding crossovers.
             b)     Ease of inter-connections between instruments.
             c)     Ease of access for on-site calibration and/ or removal of instruments.
             d)    Minimum interference between tubing, piping and cabling to instruments.
 3.9     A filter regulator with gauge shall be provided for each instrument requiring regulated gas
             or air supply.
 3.10       All open ports (vents/ drains) on field instruments including solenoid valves shall be made
              to face downwards and fitted with bug screens.
 3.11      Local mounted instruments shall be mounted on brackets, sub panels or placed on a
              suitable pedestal. They shall be easily accessible from grade, ladder or platform. Pressure
           gauges and other local indicators shall be readable from grade or operating level and if
            used for manual control, shall be visible from the related valve.
 3.12      Wherever possible, local mounted instruments shall be mounted at approximately 1.3
            meters above the platform or floor in an accessible manner. Instruments shall not impede
             process operation, e.g., masking valves, etc.
 3.13       Instruments shall be mounted as close to the sensing points as possible.
 3.14        Orifice meters shall not be installed on the top of orifice fitting, where it is necessary for a
            person to stand above it to change an orifice plate. On horizontal lines tap holes shall be as
              follows:
             a) On top for air and gas service.
            b) Bottom for liquid
